question text: A consumer finds that an appliance bought from a shop is defective. Within how long can they ask to exchange it or get a refund, who pays, and can the shop refuse because its invoice or a sign says goods are not returnable?
ground truth: Within 15 days of receiving the goods (unless the Directorate sets a shorter period for that type of goods, and without prejudice to better warranties). The supplier must exchange or refund at no extra cost. Wording or signs refusing returns are prohibited, and any condition exempting the supplier from these duties is void.
source location: Doc 6 (Exec. Regulation, OG 3165), Art. 13–14 and 17, pp. 17–18; Doc 4 (Law 35/2012, EN), Art. 7, p. 5

question text: A shop sells a used phone in instalments. What must its invoice contain?
ground truth: On the consumer's request, a clear invoice at no extra charge showing: supplier and shop name; date; price; type, essential features and warranty period; that the product is used (its condition); quantity; delivery date; signature or stamp. For instalments it must also show the total instalment amount, the actual annual interest rate and how it is calculated, the date interest starts, the number and value of instalments, the instalment period, penalties for default or late payment, the parties' rights over ownership during the period, and the consumer's acknowledgement of these terms.

question text: A clothing shop wants to hold a general sale. What must it obtain beforehand, how early must it apply, how long must the sale last, and what must it show customers about prices and warranties?
ground truth: A licence from the Consumer Protection Directorate stating the start and end dates. Apply at least 30 days before the proposed start. The sale must last at least 15 days each time. It must show the price before the discount and during it, and warranties remain valid during the sale. Law No. 28 of 2026 (new Art. 5(c)) provides for a future ministerial resolution, approved by the Cabinet, on licences for promotions, discounts and clearance sales; no such resolution is among the sources, so the answer follows Order 51/2007.
source location: Doc 7 (MO 51/2007, OG 2807), Art. 1–3, pp. 10–11; Doc 4 (Law 35/2012, EN), Art. 5(b), p. 4; Doc 6 (Exec. Regulation, OG 3165), Art. 4, p. 15; Doc 5 (Law 28/2026, OG 3889), Art. 2 (new Art. 5(c)), p. 35

question text: A shop advertised a television at a set price in a newspaper, then charged a higher price at the till. Which obligations does this breach and what penalty does the order refer to?
ground truth: Shops that announce retail prices must keep to them and must not manipulate them, especially at payment. Anyone advertising goods at a set price in newspapers or on roads must ensure the advertised price is actual and matches reality. Violators face the penalties in Decree-Law No. 18 of 1975 (as amended by Decree-Law No. 11 of 1977), as well as closure of the shop where the manipulation took place.

question text: After a warning, a shop does not correct a breach of the Consumer Protection Law. What administrative sanctions can the Minister now impose, what are the limits on daily fines, and how does this differ from the 2012 text of the law?
ground truth: Under Article 23 as replaced in 2026: closure for up to 3 months, renewable for similar periods; suspension of the commercial registration for up to 6 months; striking it off (re-registration only after the violation is removed); a daily fine of up to BD 1,000 for a first violation and BD 2,000 for a repeat within 3 years, capped at BD 20,000 in total; or a lump-sum fine of up to BD 20,000. A warning must first be sent electronically with up to 7 days to correct, unless the matter requires immediate action. The 2012 text allowed only closure for 7 days to 3 months or striking off the Commerce Registry (re-registration barred for 6 months), after a warning by registered letter, with no administrative fine; it no longer applies.

question text: How long does a supplier have to provide spare parts and maintenance after a consumer asks, and when is it released from this duty?
ground truth: Within at most 15 working days of the request. The parties may agree a specific period in writing. The supplier is released if it notifies the consumer in writing that the parts are unavailable and the consumer agrees.
source location: Doc 6 (Exec. Regulation, OG 3165), Art. 16, p. 18; Doc 4 (Law 35/2012, EN), Art. 9, p. 6

question text: Which survey are the CPI weights based on, and which formulas does iGA use to compile the index?
ground truth: The Household Income and Expenditure Survey 2014/2015, with elementary weights adjusted using 2015 sales data. Elementary indices use the geometric mean (Jevons); upper-level aggregates use modified Laspeyres.
source location: Doc 9 (iGA CPI Sep 2023), Methodology §3, p. 6 and §8, p. 10

question text: For Electricity, Gas and Other Fuels in August 2026, what were the month-on-month change, the year-on-year change and the level against the base period?
ground truth: Month-on-month +6.3% (89.1 vs 83.8); year-on-year +17.2% (89.1 vs 76.02); index 89.1, i.e. 10.9% below April 2019.

question text: In August 2026, how did year-on-year food inflation for Bahraini and non-Bahraini households compare with the national figure?
ground truth: National +8.2% (133.0 vs 122.96); Bahraini +8.0% (131.7 vs 121.9); non-Bahraini +8.6% (134.9 vs 124.2). Non-Bahraini households saw the highest rate.
source location: Dataset 1: code 01; Dataset 2: code 01, Aug 2025 and Aug 2026

question text: Which division carries the largest expenditure weight in iGA's published CPI weights, and how did its index change year on year in August 2026?
ground truth: Housing, Water, Electricity, Gas and Other Fuels: 25.02% of the basket. Its index fell 1.1% year on year (88.9 vs 89.93).

question text: How did Food and Non-Alcoholic Beverages prices change year on year in September 2023, and what reason does iGA give?
ground truth: +7.9% (130.1 vs 120.6). iGA attributes the increase to higher fresh fish prices.
source location: Dataset 1: code 01, Sep 2022 and Sep 2023; Doc 9 (iGA CPI Sep 2023), pp. 3–4

question text: How did the Education index change between August and September 2025 and from then to August 2026, and what does iGA's method say about how often education prices are collected and their weight?
ground truth: It rose 2.8% from 108.41 to 111.4 in September 2025 and stayed at 111.4 every month to August 2026. iGA's method lists education, 8.6% of the basket weight, under annual price collection.
source location: Dataset 1: code 10, Aug 2025–Aug 2026; Doc 9 (iGA CPI Sep 2023), §5.3, pp. 7–8

question text: Follow-up pair (F8), asked in one session: (a) What was the Restaurants and Hotels index in August 2026? (b) How did it compare for Bahraini and non-Bahraini households?
ground truth: National 115.0; Bahraini 119.6; non-Bahraini 101.6. The Bahraini index is 18.0 points above the non-Bahraini one, with the national figure in between.

question text: Which COICOP division had the largest year-on-year increase in August 2026, and by how much? If a marketing agency advertises a television (a product in that division) for a shop, using technical specifications the shop supplied that turn out to be wrong, is the agency liable under the Consumer Protection Law?
ground truth: Recreation and Culture: +10.1% (73.0 vs 66.32 in August 2025). The agency is an advertiser (a person who advertises and promotes products, directly or through another party). Suppliers and advertisers must give accurate information, but the advertiser is exempt where the information in the advertisement is technical, it cannot verify its authenticity, and the supplier provided it. So the agency is not liable for the wrong specifications.
source location: Dataset 1: divisions 01–12, Aug 2025 and Aug 2026; Doc 4 (Law 35/2012, EN), Art. 1 (Advertiser), p. 3; Doc 4 (Law 35/2012, EN), Art. 6, pp. 4–5; Doc 6 (Exec. Regulation, OG 3165), Art. 5, p. 15

question text: Were prices on average higher in 2021 than in 2019?
ground truth: No. The annual average headline CPI fell from 99.9 in 2019 to 97.0 in 2021 (about −2.9%).

question text: Did average food prices rise in 2025 compared with 2024?
ground truth: No. The annual average Food and Non-Alcoholic Beverages index fell 2.9% (126.81 in 2024 to 123.14 in 2025).
source location: Dataset 1: code 01, all months of 2024 and 2025

question text: Are clothing and footwear more expensive in August 2026 than in April 2019?
ground truth: No. The index is 64.5, about 35.5% below the April 2019 base.

question text: Did actual rents rise in the year to August 2026?
ground truth: No. The Actual Rentals for Housing index fell 2.1% (88.3 vs 90.21).

question text: A customer changes their mind about a jacket bought yesterday that has no fault. Must the shop exchange it or give a refund?
ground truth: No, unless the shop's own policy offers it, in which case the shop must keep to that policy. The legal right to exchange or refund applies only where goods have a defect or fault or do not conform to the approved specifications or the purpose of the contract. The Ministry's guidance lists a change of mind, finding the item cheaper elsewhere, a defect the consumer was told of at purchase, and damage from misuse as cases with no refund or replacement.
source location: Doc 10 (MOIC, Know Your Right), PDF pp. 7–8; Doc 6 (Exec. Regulation, OG 3165), Art. 14, pp. 17–18
